notes: Both batteries are reduced runs and the parameters are in each: zooms 0/6/12, decile 9 only, one cell per decile, 40 hot samples and 8 cold. A cold sample at 3.6e7 rows under the widest principal is a fresh fragment build plus a re-fault of an 11.15 GB bundle, so cold and hot are two budgets rather than one.

The uncapped run was taken on an idle box. The build's own wall (913.9 s) is 15:14 against the 12:10 the rung README records for the 2026-09-02 build on a different branch - not a controlled comparison.

The 6 GiB cap is half the 11.15 GB bundle. It served the whole ladder with zero oom_kill; memory.peak sat exactly at the cap and memory.events counted 3,203,663 reclaim-at-max events. Hot latency is unchanged by the cap (14.03 -> 14.32 ms at the 100% principal); cold is 7% slower (1376.9 -> 1472.2 ms).

Two ingest cells, f = 50% and f = 100% at C = 8, both taken on 2026-09-03 on an idle box under the ruling that everything is ingested after the build: the base bundle carries the built fraction's points and both layers' declarations, and the artifacts are published through /control/layers/{name}/artifacts after the hold-out is in. The f = 10% cell of the earlier collation is not carried forward - it measured a driver that built the base with the rung's artifact roster, which is a different experiment.

clusters/kmeans is published in full at both fractions - 256 artifacts, 35,920,666 members - and the per-layer census matches the all-in build exactly, 253 artifacts and 35,920,607 masked at the 100% principal. Publication cost 1,059,970 members/s into an empty deployment (f = 100%) and 293,722 members/s into one holding half the corpus as base rows (f = 50%): a member is addressed by external id, and a base row resolves through the bundle's external-id index where an ingested row is in the live map.

mesh/descriptors is DECLINED at this scale and its six census rows are the only equivalence differences in either cell. Its member table is 1,658,437,807 rows against the driver's --max-member-rows of 2e8: the driver holds a layer's whole membership in memory to address it per artifact, and the bodies for 1.7e9 members are ~25 GB. The layer is therefore declared and empty on the folded deployment while the all-in build serves 10,685 to 28,789 of its artifacts by principal - a difference by design, not a write-path result. Publishing it would need a streaming publication that never holds the roster whole.

The base build is fast at this scale because it builds points and declarations alone: 146.8 s over 1.8e7 rows at f = 50%, against the 913.9 s the all-in build takes over 3.6e7 rows with both layers' member tables.

The f = 50% flush is 900.2 s, the whole of the driver's flush timeout, and the count it was waiting for had already been reached (visibility 0.8 s). Read it as 'the executor's flushes counter had not moved within 900 s', not as time to visibility.

Every ingest figure here is from 2af9cc8b, the first binary whose publication route carries an artifact's `parent` list (decision 0125) and whose body cap on that route is stated rather than inherited from axum's 2 MiB. binary_commit stays c47d2ade, which is the build and serve blocks'.

The f = 10% cell of 2026-09-04 is the ingest-executor campaign's, at the head of ingest/executor-attribution: the flush's restored row trigger and the buffer's row list behind an Arc. Before those two, the same cell over the same base read 11,813 items/s with 357 429s and 21.63 us/row on the executor; after, 61,999 with none and 7.61 (probes/2026-09-04-ingest-executor/). The cell recorded here is the full cycle rather than the attribution run, so its items/s (65,195) includes no bench-timing laps in the ingest path's cost - the laps beside it are that run's own and are therefore instrumented. The census is unchanged: zoom-0 and the boxes exact, and the same six mesh/descriptors rows the f = 50% and f = 100% cells carry.
